title: In-order traversal
summary: Left, node, right: recursion visits a tree in sorted order.

checkpoints.text: The tree is built: 40 at the root, 20 and 60 below it, 10 and 30 under 20. Now `inOrder` will visit every node.
The calls went left, left, left until `node` was nullptr. Look at the stack: one frame for 40, one for 20, one for 10, and this empty one, which returns at once.
Back in the frame for 10. Its left side is done, so 10 prints first: it is the smallest value.
40, the root, prints fourth. Its whole left subtree (10, 20, 30) had to finish first.
Every node printed exactly once, and in sorted order: 10 20 30 40 60. For a binary search tree, in-order traversal always gives sorted output.
`destroy` is another traversal, post-order: both children are deleted before their parent. The first node deleted is the leaf 10.
